blacklistabilityReview.sourceFreeRationale: Explicit true: a live authorized burner (the Mento Broker) can directly burn an arbitrary holder balance, and the owner Safe can authorize further burners or operators that move holder balances without allowance. This direct freeze/blacklist-equivalent capability is distinct from the transfer-review lane and does not suppress the upstream reserve-basket exposure.
blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Write-time re-read at Celo block 73546760 (2026-07-30): the EURm proxy 0xd8763cba276a3738e6de85b4b3bf5fded6d6ca73 resolves to the Blockscout-verified StableTokenV3 implementation 0x815795c30d0758a297b08cd4e0643620c974c318 and owner() returned the Mento Safe 0x58099B74F4ACd642Da77b4B7966b4138ec5Ba458 (Safe API at write time: threshold 4, 6 owners). isBurner(0x777A8255cA72412f0d706dc03C9D1987306B4CaD) returned true: the Mento Broker is a live burner and can call burn(address account, uint256 value) against an arbitrary holder balance without allowance. The verified source also exposes owner-gated setBurner(address,bool) and setOperator(address,bool); an enabled operator can sendToPool(sender,pool,amount) from an arbitrary holder. The observed burner uses constrained protocol paths, but the owner Safe can authorize another burner or operator. This establishes a current direct individual-holder intervention capability even though the ABI has no named blacklist, freeze, or pause function. Same implementation and verdict as the reviewed chfm-mento precedent.

oracleRisk.summary: At Celo block 78986505, EURm uses 2 registered Celo V3 FPMMs. Every reviewed rateFeedID has one authorized ChainlinkRelayerV1 reporter and one current getRates entry: SortedOracles is a sorted-list median, not redundant live price failover. Effective report expiry is 360 seconds (global default 300). The axlEUROC/EURm pool 0x3aa7c431c06b10f7422e69d3e69b66807a6af696 uses feed 0x26076b9702885d475ac8c3db3bd9f250dc5a318b and relayer 0x72fa4feab8225a234325dccb79862a0ad3ca4fb9. Its two Chainlink aggregator segments multiply EUROC/USD by inverted EUR/USD; they are a composite conversion, not alternatives (maximum timestamp spread 300 seconds). ValueDeltaBreaker is enabled at 0.5%, reference 1e24 and one-second reset cooldown; MedianDelta is disabled. LP/protocol fees are 30/20 basis points. USDm/EURm uses the single-reporter EUR/USD feed 0xf4f9bbda9cd6841fcb9b1510f9269e2db42a6e3a, MedianDelta 4%/900 seconds, LP/protocol fees 15/10 basis points. FPMMs read OracleAdapter.getFXRateIfValid on quotes/swaps. Stable collateral pools use adapter 0xeb23e1339b2119c0f4a0097cb294e990c1fa6423 with always-open market-hours configuration; FX pools use 0xa472fbbf4b890a54381977ac392bdf82eec4383a with FX hours. Both reject stale medians or non-bidirectional BreakerBox modes and have no alternative live feed. Breaker cooldowns are reset waits, not price observation or liquidation delays. All pinned rates were recent and returned nonzero quotes. The tier follows the existing Mento single-source-or-laggy convention, not the former unsupported failover claim.

branchApplicability.rationale: EURm is explicitly reserve-backed in the pinned issuer configuration, not one of the GBPm/CHFm/JPYm CDP assets. The enumerated pinned FPMM swap/rebalancing paths has external price authority but no borrower-specific liquidation engine. Score this authority as coin-price-feed/top-level-only; branch rows and liquidationDelaySec are not applicable. A 900-second breaker reset cooldown or 360-second report expiry is not a liquidation delay. This review covers canonical Celo exchange pricing and does not classify separate bridge control or remote-chain liquidity.

Its deployed quote/swap implementation calls getFXRateIfValid and applies pool fees; it is a spot pool and reserve-liquidity pricing authority, not a borrower liquidation engine for EURm. The pinned issuer configuration explicitly identifies EURm as reserve-backed. This exact FPMM pricing path is top-level-only; pairing with a CDP-backed token does not create a local borrower branch for this reserve-backed asset.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Celo native EURm is the canonical route; Monad is a Wormhole NTT burn/mint representation. Mento's official NTT configuration sets nominal 500,000 EURm inbound and outbound limits per peer, and the common 4-of-6 migration Safe 0x58099B74F4ACd642Da77b4B7966b4138ec5Ba458 can administer the Celo and Monad NTT manager/transceiver contracts. These are nominal configured limits, not live remaining-capacity reads. The residual Ethereum and Polygon supply is legacy Optics-bridged cEUR (token owner is the Optics BridgeRouter, verified on-chain), and the Solana supply is legacy Allbridge cEUR (mint authority verified). Pinned totalSupply reads on 2026-07-21 establish 2,073,193.841739276070272578 unique EURm/cEUR claims: 1,688,715.972819276070272578 in the Celo canonical supply, including the backing of legacy lock-mint representations, plus 384,477.868920000000000000 on the Monad NTT burn-mint deployment. Monad therefore carries 18.54519636% of unique claims, so the chain:monad common-mode exposure is attributed and remains above the 10% materiality threshold.
